$meta.name: JRK Analytics Design Tokens
$meta.description: Single source of truth. Run `npm run build` to regenerate dist/. Never hand-edit dist/.
$meta.look: Apple. macOS/iOS grouped surfaces, system greys, a stepped-blue accent at hue 212deg (deeper than systemBlue, which fails as a label and as link text), Inter as the SF stand-in, compact non-touch density for 1920x1080 desktop.
$meta.$surfaceNote: LIGHT no longer separates its planes by fill: page and card are both #ffffff, and the 2px border.card edge is the entire tile boundary. DARK keeps the Apple grouped fill hierarchy (#141416 page, #1c1c1e card) with the same edge on top of it. The chart surface is still the CARD in both modes — #ffffff light, #1c1c1e dark — which in light is now numerically identical to the page but is a different fact, and marks are measured against the card.
$meta.$appleNote: Values are Apple's system colours verbatim wherever they clear WCAG. Where Apple's own value fails — systemGray as body text is 2.92:1, three of four status marks are under 3:1 on light — the token is darkened and the deviation is noted on the token.
$meta.validated: Categorical palette passes the dataviz six-checks in both modes on both pairlists. Run `npm run validate` after any color change.

ramp.$comment: Apple system greys and the systemIndigo family. Semantic tokens below reference these; components never reference a ramp step directly.

neutral.$comment: systemGray6 -> systemGray, then the dark-mode greys. Light half is Apple's light system greys; 700 and below are Apple's dark system greys.

color.$comment: Semantic color tokens. Every entry has a light and dark value; dark is SELECTED for the dark surface, never computed from light.

surface.$comment: BOTH themes now separate their planes by the same mechanism: an Apple grouped FILL STEP, page to card, with no border involved. Light is #f2f2f7 page / #ffffff card (1.12:1); dark is #141416 page / #232326 card (1.17:1). That symmetry is new and it is the point — for one period this library ran a flat white light page bounded by a 2px brand edge, which meant a change that read correctly in dark could be invisible in light. There is no longer a per-theme boundary mechanism to get wrong. What replaces the edge for interactive tiles is a hover SHADOW, not a border; see shadow.md and .jrk-card--interactive.

canvas.$lightNote: systemGroupedBackground, and the tinted plane the grouped look is built on. This value was briefly #ffffff, paired with a 2px brand edge on every tile that did the entire job of bounding it. Both halves of that pair are now gone together, which is the only safe way to undo it: the page is tinted again, so the 1.12:1 step to the white card IS the tile boundary and no border is needed. Restored by the same change: .jrk-card--seamless has a boundary in light again, and .jrk-content--document is no longer a no-op there. Note the step is small in ratio terms — 1.12:1 is a fill relationship, not a contrast one, and WCAG has nothing to say about it. It is legal because no information depends on seeing it: a card's CONTENT carries the meaning, the fill only groups it.
canvas.$darkNote: NOT #000000. iOS grouped dark uses true black, but on a 1920x1080 desktop it produces halation against near-white text and reads as a void rather than a page — macOS window backgrounds sit near #1e1e1e for exactly this reason. #141416 is ramp neutral-925. When the brand edge was removed this value was deliberately LEFT ALONE and the card was lifted instead (see surface.default): darkening the page would have widened the same step while re-opening a halation question that was already measured and settled.

default.$darkNote: Was #1c1c1e (Apple's secondarySystemGroupedBackground), which sat a mere 1.08:1 off the page and leaned on the 2px brand edge to be legible as a tile at all. With the edge gone the fill has to do the whole job, so the card was lifted to #232326 — a 1.17:1 step, which is actually stronger than the light theme's 1.12:1. Lifting the card rather than darkening the page keeps the settled #141416 halation decision untouched. Two tokens had to move with it: surface.disabled.dark, which was #242426 and would now be invisible ON the card, and focus.offset.dark, which names this surface.
default.$darkCostNote: Lifting the card costs contrast for everything drawn ON it, because the card IS the chart surface. Every dark chart series mark lost about 8%: worst case is slot 1 blue (#0a84ff) at 4.66:1 -> 4.30:1, and slots 5 and 6 at 4.83:1 -> 4.45:1. All eight still clear the mark floor and the validator reports no new warnings. Text is unaffected in practice — text.primary is 14.3:1 -> 13.19:1. Recorded because this is the cost side of the trade, and if surface.default is ever lifted again these are the numbers that will run out first.

tinted.use: KPI band, highlighted tiles — soft brand wash

track.use: the recessed well of a segmented control / pill tabs — .jrk-btn-group and .jrk-tabs--pills
track.$note: Its own token because there is no longer a general one that is recessed in BOTH themes. The track used to be surface.subtle, which was #f2f2f7 in light; the light-page flattening moved subtle to #ffffff, so the well became the same colour as the card it sits on and the control lost its anatomy silently. Recessed by 1.22:1 in light and 1.13:1 in dark — the same order as the card's own fill step, so it reads as an inset without becoming a box. Dark is #18181a rather than #1a1a1c to stay off surface.disabled.dark; the two would otherwise be the same value in different roles. The binding measurement is the SELECTED pill against this: accent.solid is 4.28:1 on the light track and 3.40:1 on the dark one, both clear of the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a state indicator.

surface.$removedThumbNote: surface.thumb (#ffffff / #48484a) is GONE, along with the white floating thumb it drew. Its own `use` string declared the invariant that killed it — 'must be LIGHTER than the track in both modes' — and in light it had become #ffffff on a #ffffff track: 1.00:1, no step whatsoever, with a 0.5px shadow as the only evidence a segment was selected. That is a signifier failure rather than a style problem, because something DOES depend on seeing which segment is selected, and the same reasoning is already written on border.accent for the tab underline. The selected segment now takes accent.solid with accent.onSolid ink and semibold, which is the treatment .jrk-nav-item[aria-current] already uses for 'this is the active one' — three channels instead of a shadow. If a white-thumb segmented control is ever wanted back, it needs a track dark enough for white to clear 3:1 on it, which is a much darker well than Apple's.

banner.use: sheet title bar — the one heavy element in a dense report
banner.$lightNote: Tracks accent.solid: #5856d6 -> #9ee4ff -> #0069d9. It is a DARK surface again in light mode, so text.onBanner and text.onBannerMuted went back to white with it. This is the largest area the accent covers anywhere in the product, which is why it is the token that exposes an accent's lightness fastest — the pastel made the report's heaviest element its palest, and this reverses that. Dark stays neutral #2c2c2e throughout and has never moved.

hover.$lightNote: Equals surface.canvas in light, which is correct for a ROW inside a card (it recedes toward the page) and wrong for a whole TILE — washing a white card with the page colour erases the fill step that bounds it. That is what cardHover below exists for; do not use this token on a card.

raisedHover.use: row hover INSIDE a raised surface — menus, the select popup, the daterange list
raisedHover.$note: surface.hover cannot do this job and failed silently for as long as menus have existed: surface.hover.dark and surface.raised.dark are the SAME value (#2c2c2e), so `.jrk-menu__item:hover` painted a menu row with the exact colour of the menu under it and dark mode had no hover feedback at all. Nothing catches this — the validator measures text and marks, never a wash against the plane it washes. This is the same class of trap as surface.cardHover, which exists because surface.hover erases the fill step that bounds a card. Both are surface.hover being wrong for one specific plane. Light is #f2f2f7, identical to surface.hover, because raised.light is #ffffff and the ordinary step works there — the two modes agree by coincidence, not by rule, so re-measure if surface.raised moves. Dark is a 1.140:1 lift off the raised plane, chosen to match the light pair's 1.116:1 rather than to look right in isolation, and it stays 1.077:1 clear of surface.active so hover and pressed do not collapse into each other.

cardHover.use: fill of an INTERACTIVE card while hovered — see .jrk-card--interactive:hover
cardHover.$note: The two themes deliberately disagree about whether this token does anything, because the shadow that accompanies it only works in one of them. In LIGHT it is a no-op (identical to surface.default) and the hover shadow carries the whole affordance — any tint here would pull the card toward the page and dissolve its boundary at the moment it is meant to respond. In DARK the shadow is nearly invisible (a black shadow on a #141416 page, as noted on the shadow tokens), so the fill has to carry it: #2c2c2e is a 1.125:1 lift off the card. One CSS rule, one token, a real affordance in both themes — which is the alternative to branching the stylesheet on theme.

disabled.$darkNote: This token has now been broken twice by a surface.default move, both times silently, because disabled fills are exempt from the contrast gate and nothing checks them. First it was #1c1c1e, identical to the card, so a disabled control on a card had no fill at all. Then #242426 — which is 1.01:1 against the card's NEW #232326, the same bug again. #1a1a1c is chosen the other way round: it RECEDES from the card at 1.109:1, which is what the light pair does (#f2f2f7 on #ffffff, 1.12:1). Matching the light relationship instead of the light direction is what makes it stable — if surface.default moves again, check this token.

text.$comment: Apple label colours where they pass. muted is DARKER than Apple's systemGray (#8e8e93) on purpose — systemGray measures 2.92:1 on the canvas and fails AA as body text. Apple accepts that for tertiary labels; we do not.

primary.$darkNote: Apple's dark label is pure white, and that is the one place the value is adopted and then backed off. #ffffff on the #1c1c1e card measures 15.9:1 and on the old black page 21:1 — far past AA, and the excess shows up as glare and halation on 42px semibold hero figures. #ebebf0 is Apple's own dark secondaryLabel base tint at ~92% white: 14.3:1 on the card, 15.5:1 on the page, still triple the 4.5:1 floor.

secondary.use: supporting copy, labels — Apple secondaryLabel base

muted.use: axis ticks, captions, placeholders — darkened from systemGray to clear 4.5:1

disabled.use: disabled label — decorative only, never load-bearing

link.use: inline links, accent text — tracks accent.text
link.$lightNote: The brand hex, which it was not under the pastel accent. 5.22:1 on the white card, 4.68:1 on the #f2f2f7 page. The page is the binding surface and it is easy to miss: the anchor was pinned against it, and a blue that looks fine on the white card can fail there.

onBanner.$note: White in both modes again, having spent the pastel era as dark ink (#052f3b) in light. It follows surface.banner, which follows accent.solid: the band went from a pale #9ee4ff back to a saturated #0069d9, so the label went back with it. 5.22:1 on the light band, 15.02:1 on the dark neutral one. The two modes agree in direction once more, but for a reason that can lapse again — check this token whenever accent.solid moves.

onBannerMuted.$lightNote: A near-white tint, not a grey, and the band is why: white on #0069d9 is only 5.22:1, so there is 0.72 of headroom between onBanner and the 4.5:1 floor for this token to be muted INTO. #e8f1fd spends most of it at 4.58:1. It reads as muted next to white, but the light banner is the tightest type pairing in the file — a genuinely grey label cannot pass there. If the banner ever needs a real muted step, deepen surface.banner rather than lightening this.

border.$comment: Apple separators, and now the ONLY border namespace — there is no longer a brand edge on a tile. A card-like tile is bounded by its FILL STEP off the page in both themes (1.12:1 light, 1.17:1 dark), so these values are for internal rules, input borders, popover edges, and the neutral hairline a NESTED tile takes when it has no page to step off. In dark the hairline does more work than in light because the fill steps are shallower there in absolute terms; both dark steps are lifted off Apple's systemGray5/4 for that reason.
border.$removedNote: border.card is GONE, and so is size.cardEdge. It was a 2px #48a9df brand line on every outermost tile — the one deliberate break from Apple in this file — and it existed because the light page had been flattened to #ffffff and nothing else bounded a tile there. The page is tinted again, so the reason is gone with it. Removing the token rather than leaving it unused is deliberate: it was documented as THE brand line, and a dead brand token in the source of truth is an invitation to put it back on something. This is a BREAKING removal for any consumer that referenced --jrk-border-card or --jrk-card-edge directly.

subtle.$darkNote: Was #2c2c2e, which is 1.22:1 on the old #1c1c1e card — a rule that vanished at desktop viewing distance. #333336 measures 1.31:1 on the current #232326 card.

default.use: input borders, popover edges, and the NESTED-tile hairline — systemGray4 / opaqueSeparator
default.$darkNote: Lifted from #38383a for the same reason as subtle.

strong.use: axis, baselines, dividers needing weight — opaqueSeparator

accent.$lightNote: A tab underline is a non-text signifier under WCAG 1.4.11, so it needs 3:1, and something DOES depend on seeing this one (which tab is selected). Under the pastel this token had to carry its own bespoke step (#0096cf, 3.00:1 on the page — barely) because the anchor was 1.40:1. It now takes accent.text unchanged at 4.68:1 on the page and 5.22:1 on the card, so the special case is gone. Keep it tracking accent.text rather than re-deriving it: the floor it has to clear is lower than text's, so text is always the safe value.

accent.$comment: A blue brand at hue 212deg, anchored on #0069d9. This is the second replacement: systemIndigo (#5856d6) -> a #9ee4ff cyan pastel -> this. It reverts the inversion the pastel forced. #0069d9 is a SATURATED MID-TONE, so it behaves the way an accent normally does — white sits on it (5.22:1), it reads as text on both light surfaces (5.22:1 card, 4.68:1 page), and it clears the 3:1 signifier floor everywhere. The three roles that the pastel had to route around — border.accent, focus.ring, text.link — now all take the anchor itself, which is the whole point of the change. Not Apple's systemBlue: #007aff gives white only 4.02:1 as a label and 3.60:1 as link text on the page, so it fails here exactly the way systemGray and systemIndigo do. #0069d9 is the shallowest step on the hue that clears 4.5:1 in every light-mode role. Dark takes a SELECTED lighter step for text roles (#64b5ff) and keeps the anchor for fills, because a fill and a glyph do not want the same value on a #232326 card.

solid.use: primary button fill, selected nav pill
solid.$note: The brand anchor, verbatim, and the same value in both modes — a saturated mid-tone needs no per-theme selection because its label is white in both. On the dark card it sits at 3.00:1, which clears the non-text floor, so the fill's own boundary reads without a border.

solidHover.$note: Deepens on hover, same direction as the pastel it replaces but for the ordinary reason: a saturated fill darkens under the pointer. White on it is 6.18:1.

solidActive.$note: Deeper again. White on it is 6.87:1, so the label GAINS contrast through the press sequence 5.22 -> 6.18 -> 6.87. The pastel ran the same sequence in the opposite direction (12.15 -> 8.71 -> 7.69) because it was deepening toward its ink rather than away from it.

onSolid.use: label ON the solid accent — WHITE in both modes
onSolid.$note: This token has now been white, then dark ink (#052f3b, for the pastel era), then white again. The rule is not 'white' or 'dark' — it is 'whatever measures against accent.solid', and the value follows the anchor's lightness. It is still NOT text.inverse: text.inverse is #ffffff in light and #000000 in DARK, for the inverse surface, so the two agree in light and disagree in dark. They have been separate facts through all three accents. Do not collapse them. Do not borrow this token as a generic 'label on a filled control' either — .jrk-btn--danger-solid used to, and the red fill silently inherited the accent's ink direction; that is what status.critical.solid/onSolid now exist for.

text.$lightNote: The brand anchor unchanged — this is the first accent in the library's history where the anchor IS the light-mode text value. 5.22:1 on the white card, 4.68:1 on the #f2f2f7 page. The page is still the binding surface, so it is what pins the anchor: a blue tuned only to the white card can sit a full step lighter and fail on the page.
text.$darkNote: #64b5ff is selected, not derived from the anchor — #0069d9 is 3.00:1 on the dark card and cannot be text there. 7.16:1 on the card, 8.41:1 on the page.

wash.use: selected row tint, soft badge fill

washText.$note: Light is stepped deeper than accent.text, not equal to it: the wash is a tint, so text on it has less room than on the white card. The anchor itself lands at 4.49:1 on #e3efff — under the floor by 0.01, which is the clearest possible demonstration of why this token is separate. #005ec4 (the solidHover step) is 5.31:1. Dark reuses accent.text on the deep wash at 6.73:1.

status.$comment: Apple system colours for the marks; darkened steps for text, because Apple's own systemGreen/Orange/Yellow fail 4.5:1 as text on white. Reserved meanings — never reused as a chart series, which is why green and red are held out of the categorical palette entirely.

solid.use: fill of the ONE filled destructive button — .jrk-btn--danger-solid, never a status mark
solid.$note: A separate, deeper red from status.critical.mark, and it exists because of a coupling that went unnoticed for three accents. .jrk-btn--danger-solid used to fill with the MARK and label it with accent.onSolid — so the red button's ink direction was decided by the accent, and every accent change moved it silently. Nothing gates it: the validator measures status text on the surface and on the wash, never a label on a mark. Under the pastel it sat at 4.01:1 and would have dropped to 3.55:1 when onSolid went back to white. The mark itself cannot be relabelled white either — #ff3b30 gives white 3.55:1. This value is the shallowest deepening of systemRed where white clears 4.5:1 (5.09:1), and it still reads as the same red at a glance. It sits 3.08:1 on the dark card, so it does not need a border in either mode. Same value both modes for the same reason accent.solid is.

onSolid.$note: Its own token rather than a reach for accent.onSolid or text.inverse. text.inverse is #000000 in dark and would put black on a red button there; accent.onSolid is the coupling this pair was created to break.

focus.$comment: Apple's focus ring is a soft accent halo rather than a hard outline. base.css draws it as a 3px ring at reduced alpha plus a 1px solid core.

ring.use: focus ring core — must clear 3:1 on page, card, and inset well
ring.$lightNote: The brand anchor itself, which under the pastel accent was an accessibility failure rather than a style choice (#9ee4ff is 1.40:1 on the card). A focus ring is the single most load-bearing signifier in a keyboard path, so it takes the anchor only because the anchor measures: 5.22:1 card, 4.68:1 page, 4.68:1 inset well. Dark takes accent.text at 6.37:1 on the darkest of the three.

offset.use: ring offset, so the ring reads on any surface
offset.$darkNote: Names surface.default and has to move with it — was #1c1c1e.

chart.$comment: Data-viz layer. Categorical order is the CVD-safety mechanism — assign slots 1..N in order, NEVER cycle. A 9th series folds into 'Other' or facets. Scatter/bubble/choropleth/small-multiples cap at 3 series (all-pairs validated).

categorical.$derivation: Seeded from Apple's system colours, then ordered by search to maximise the WORST ADJACENT pair across BOTH modes jointly — only neighbours touch in a stack or a line chart, and the slot->hue mapping has to be one fact or a series would change hue when the theme is toggled. Apple publishes no CVD-safe categorical sequence (systemRed beside systemGreen is the textbook protan collapse), so the order is derived, not adopted. Blue is pinned to slot 1: it is the default single-series colour used by every bar list, cell bar and sparkline, so it has to be the neutral one — the unconstrained optimum put orange there, which reads as a warning. systemGreen and systemRed are held out entirely (status good/critical — a green or red series in a financial chart reads as a verdict) and systemIndigo is held out as the UI accent. Result: worst adjacent CVD deltaE 16.3 light / 15.1 dark, roughly double the previous palette.
categorical.$accentReservationStale: The derivation above holds systemIndigo out of the palette 'as the UI accent'. That reservation has been stale since the accent left indigo, and the ACCEPTED debt is now at its worst: the accent is a blue at hue 212deg, and slot 1 is systemBlue at 211deg. They are the same hue. Two earlier readings of this note recorded the gap as 14.6deg (cyan accent vs slot 1) and 7.6deg (cyan accent vs slot 7 teal); it is now about 1deg, against the ONE slot that matters most, because slot 1 is the default single-series colour used by every bar list, cell bar and sparkline. This was a deliberate call, not an oversight: re-deriving the order means re-running the joint light/dark CVD search across all eight slots and re-colouring every chart in the product, and Apple's own consoles ship blue bars beside blue buttons. What separates them is LIGHTNESS only — accent.solid #0069d9 gives white 5.22:1, slot 1 #007aff gives white 4.02:1 — which is a real but thin distinction, thinner than the one the cyan accent had. Consequences to respect until it is resolved: never put a chart on an accent wash; never let a chart's single blue series sit adjacent to a primary button in the same tile without a label between them; and if a ninth series is ever needed, resolve this properly instead of extending the order.
categorical.$redundancy: Every slot carries THREE channels, not one: hue, dash, and shape. Hue alone is only safe for ADJACENT marks. The order was searched to maximise the worst adjacent pair, and the arithmetic consequence is that similar hues get pushed four slots apart — so every pair that collapses under simulated CVD is (n, n+4): orange|yellow deltaE 0.8, mint|teal 1.8 dark, blue|purple 4.4, pink|brown 3.9, measured Machado 2009 severity 1.0 + CIEDE2000 against a floor of 10. Anything comparing NON-adjacent series needs the second channel. dash and shape are assigned so all four (n, n+4) pairs and the (2,4) pair differ in both.
categorical.$barsExemptNote: Bars deliberately have no per-slot channel. .jrk-bars is single-series (slot 1) and .jrk-stack-bar segments are adjacent by construction, so hue alone is sufficient there and the existing 45/135 texture alternation is the right shape for it — chart.css restricts hatching to those two angles because horizontal and vertical read as gridlines, which leaves too few textures to separate (n, n+4) anyway. If a GROUPED bar chart is ever added it puts slot 2 beside slot 4, and it must carry direct labels or the shape channel; alternating texture cannot save it, because n and n+4 always share parity.
categorical.$dashNote: Slot 1 is solid on purpose: it is the default single-series colour and a lone chart must not look provisional. Dash applies to line marks only, and only under the redundancy switch — charts.md reserves dashed strokes for .jrk-threshold, so a dashed SERIES line is legal only where the author opted in. See the conflict register in philosophy.md.

slots.apple: systemYellow, darkened into the lightness band
systemBrown, chroma raised to clear the floor

reliefRequired.note: Sub-3:1 on the white card. Apple's system colours are bright, and a white card is the least forgiving surface for them. Ship visible direct labels or the table view when these are fills. Not dismissable.

tint.$comment: Pastel fills for LARGE marks whose identity is already carried by an axis label, a direct value label, or a number in the legend. Deliberately outside the lightness band and under the chroma floor, so they cannot do identity work and the validator skips them. Using a tint where color IS the identity channel is a bug no gate will catch.
tint.rule: legal only when the mark is axis-labelled, direct-labelled, or accompanied by a value in the legend

ink.use: label set inside a tint fill

ordinalFloor.note: Ordinal ramps must clear 2:1 vs surface. The white card is less forgiving than a tinted one, so the light floor sits deeper than it would on a grey page.

diverging.note: systemRed <-> systemBlue with a NEUTRAL grey midpoint. Equal step count per arm. Never a hue at the midpoint, never a rainbow.

steps.$comment: Four steps per arm, for tinting a TABLE CELL by signed value (.jrk-cell-heat). The poles above are mark colours for a chart; these are fills that sit UNDER text, which is a different job with a harder constraint. Red<->blue rather than red<->green is the whole reason this pair exists: red beside green is the textbook protan collapse, and polarity is exactly the signal you cannot afford to lose. Derived and gated, not eyeballed — `validate` measures all four properties below and fails on any of them.
steps.$constraint: A heat cell carries its own number, so text.primary must clear 4.5:1 on EVERY step in BOTH themes. That is what caps the ramp's darkness in light and its lightness in dark, and it is why neither arm ever reaches its pole: the light arm stops at #ff9c93 (black 10.43:1) and the dark arm at #2f68a1 (#ebebf0 at 4.89:1, the binding value in this whole block). Push either arm one step further for 'more contrast' and the number inside it goes illegible.
steps.$separation: Polarity must survive CVD, because on a signed table the arm IS the meaning. Worst pair is rank 1 in light at deltaE 13.0 (protanopia); every other rank runs 19.5 -> 38.8. Rank 1 was deliberately re-stepped from a paler pair that measured 9.8 and sat under the floor of 10 — the near-zero band is where polarity matters least, but an exception there would still have been an exception.
steps.$rampVsIdentity: Do NOT apply the categorical CVD floor to CONSECUTIVE steps within an arm — they run deltaE 4.2-6.5 and that is correct, not a failure. Adjacent steps in a magnitude ramp are supposed to be similar; that similarity is what makes it read as a ramp. The floor exists for categorical identity, where a reader must name which series a mark belongs to. Here the reader decodes magnitude across the range and the exact value is printed in the cell.

chrome.$comment: surface is the CARD, not the page — that is what chart marks sit on and what the validator measures against.

family.$comment: Inter first, everywhere. SF Pro cannot be shipped — no webfont, and the outlines are Apple's — so the previous SF-first stack meant Apple hardware and Windows rendered in different typefaces, and the tracking below could only be right for one of them. Inter is the closest widely-available SF analogue and it is the one the library is now tuned against. -apple-system and 'Segoe UI' stay as fallbacks so a failed font load degrades to the platform UI face rather than to Arial. Delivery is css/fonts.css.
family.sans: Inter, 'Inter var', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif
family.mono: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', SFMono-Regular, Menlo, 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace

feature.$comment: Inter carries SF-ish alternates behind OpenType features; base.css applies this on body so every consumer gets the same shapes. cv05 gives lowercase l a tail, which is the one that earns its keep here — property codes and unit numbers are full of l / I / 1 and Inter's default straight l is ambiguous in all three. ss03 rounds the quotes and commas. Both are silently ignored by a font that lacks them, so the fallbacks in family.sans stay safe. Tabular figures are NOT set here — they are per-context via .jrk-tabular, because a standalone hero figure reads better proportional.

size.$comment: Apple's type ladder adapted for a dense desktop dashboard. md (14px) is body.

tracking.$comment: Negative tracking on display sizes is most of what makes type read as Apple. SF tightens optically as it grows and Inter does too — its opsz axis (14..32, requested in css/fonts.css) is what does it — so these values carry over from the SF-first stack unchanged. Do not add more negative tracking to compensate for Inter; opsz and these tokens already stack.

radius.$comment: Apple corners are TIGHTER than most web design systems — macOS controls sit near 6px and cards near 10-12px. The previous 10/14/18/24 read as friendly-web, not Apple.

shadow.$comment: Apple leans on hairlines and material, not drop shadows. These are deliberately faint. In dark mode the lightened surface and the hairline are still the primary elevation cues, but now that the page is #141416 rather than true black the dark shadows do render — faintly, which is the intent. They rendered nothing at all against black.

$shadowUsageNote: shadow.lg is the interactive-card hover raise as well as the popover elevation — see .jrk-card--interactive:hover. Elevation is still opt-in AT REST: a dashboard of tiles reads calmer flat, and every tile carrying a resting shadow was the look this system was built to avoid. The hover raise is the exception and it earns it as a layer-3 signifier: with no border on a card, a hover fill change is not available either (surface.hover.light is #f2f2f7, which equals the page, so washing a white card on hover would DISSOLVE its boundary rather than highlight it). The shadow is the only channel left that adds rather than removes definition.

size.$comment: macOS-compact, non-touch. These displays are 1920x1080 with a mouse, so the 44px touch target is dead weight — and 1080px of HEIGHT is the real constraint, which is why the vertical rhythm tightened too.
size.$removedCardEdgeNote: cardEdge (2px) is GONE with color.border.card — a tile is bounded by its fill step now, so there is no tile-edge weight to keep in one place. The five components that drew it (card, stat, stat band, chart card, sheet) each keep a 1px TRANSPARENT border instead of dropping the border shorthand entirely, so that a nested tile gaining its neutral hairline changes only a color and never reflows the layout by a pixel. Internal rules were always a hardcoded 1px and still are.
size.$minTouchNote: 24px is the WCAG 2.2 AA floor (2.5.8 Target Size Minimum), down from the 44px AAA touch target. Do not go below 24.

sheet.$comment: Spreadsheet density, tightened further for non-touch. Fixed track widths, because the Excel-style column bar can only line up with the data if every row shares one track list.
sheet.label: 98px

motion.$comment: Apple easing is a gentle ease-out; transitions are quick and small. All wrapped in the prefers-reduced-motion guard in base.css.
